claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is a homogeneously alloyed solid solution.
Controlled thermal annealing can induce subtle local atomic ordering without causing phase segregation.
Thermally induced local atomic ordering alters the ensemble of active surface sites.
Changes in active-site ensembles govern selectivity during ethanol oxidation.
Local atomic ordering facilitates a pathway that reduces formation of over-oxidized products.
Thermal annealing locally rearranges the constituent metal atoms.
Annealing enriches surface ensembles optimized for ethanol adsorption.
The enriched ensembles favor oxidation to acetaldehyde rather than further oxidation to acetate.
The ordering-induced surface modification reduces catalyst poisoning.
Reduced poisoning and suppressed over-oxidation improve catalyst durability.
Relative to the as-synthesized catalyst, the annealed catalyst will have improved selectivity for desired oxidation products.
Relative to the as-synthesized catalyst, the annealed catalyst will retain higher catalytic activity over repeated cycles.
The annealed catalyst will exhibit surface-characterization features consistent with increased local atomic ordering.
The proposed behavior is expected only within an annealing window that produces ordering without extensive sintering or phase segregation.
The magnitude of the selectivity and durability changes depends on the annealing parameters.
